threads.body: Using this group for the two realtime session events replaces their previous `server.address` description with this brief. The generated event docs therefore lose the guidance to prefer a domain name only when available without a reverse DNS lookup, and otherwise use an IP address or socket name. Please preserve that guidance in the shared brief or in event-specific overrides, then regenerate the docs.
threads.hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,99 @@
+file_format: definition/2
+attribute_groups:
+  - id: attributes.gen_ai.error
+    visibility: internal
+    attributes:
+      - ref: error.type
+        requirement_level:
+          conditionally_required: "If the operation ended in an error."
+        note: |
+          The `error.type` SHOULD match the error code returned by the Generative AI provider or the client library,
+          the canonical name of exception that occurred, or another low-cardinality error identifier.
+          Instrumentations SHOULD document the list of errors they report.
+
+  - id: attributes.gen_ai.common
+    visibility: internal
+    attributes:
+      - ref: gen_ai.request.model
+        requirement_level:
+          conditionally_required: If available.
+        note: >
+          The name of the GenAI model a request is being made to. If the model is supplied by a vendor,
+          then the value must be the exact name of the model requested. If the model is a fine-tuned
+          custom model, the value should have a more specific name than the base model that's been fine-tuned.
+      - ref: gen_ai.operation.name
+        requirement_level: required
+      - ref: gen_ai.provider.name
+        requirement_level: required
+
+  - id: attributes.gen_ai.address_and_port
+    visibility: internal
+    attributes:
+      - ref: server.address
+        brief: GenAI server address.

replies.body: it aligns realtime server address and port with what we have for the rest of genai conventions.

threads.body: Nit: now that `gen_ai.provider.name` is `required` in this shared group, a few callers lower it locally (e.g. `gen_ai.retrieval.client` → `conditionally_required: When applicable`, `gen_ai.client.operation.duration` → `conditionally_required: If the operation involves a call to a GenAI provider`). Resolved output is correct since the local ref wins, but could we add a short YAML comment here noting that signals may override this requirement level? Otherwise readers of `common.yaml` may assume it is always required.
